Jonas here, co-founder and COO of CloudKnife. As an Azure engineer and consultant, I kept seeing the same thing. Cloud bills grow, nobody knows what’s really needed, and the engineers who could fix it are busy building what matters. Now AI spend is going the same way, only faster. So Gilles, Thomas and I built CloudKnife to handle it from A to Z, for both cloud infrastructure and AI. It learns what every resource is and how it’s used. A deterministic core makes sure every recommendation is safe, and once you approve, CloudKnife makes the change. It started as an after-hours project and is now our full-time job. Real answers from real users, pulled straight from launch discussions, forums, and reviews.

### Q: Can AI agent automation platforms run scheduled multi-step workflows across apps?

Instruct can — these platforms routinely run scheduled, multi-step workflows across apps.

If you need help mapping a specific workflow, mention the apps and cadence and I can sketch a flow.

Alfie Ranstead
Alfie Ranstead
Kate Ramakaieva

### Q: Which AI agent platforms provide prebuilt OAuth connectors and enterprise security?

Merge — Connector Studio generates connectors from API docs/GitHub links and handles authentication and credential management for you, so you don’t have to build OAuth flows yourself. [...] # The Best AI Workflow Automation Tools

AI automation tools help design and run workflows that actually take action, not just suggest what to do next, allowing users to automate workflows efficiently.

AI workflow automation quietly crossed a line this year. Not because the AI tools became flashier, but because they became dependable. Teams stopped treating them as experiments and started trusting them with real work.

Across Product Hunt reviews, the language shifted. Less focus on agents in theory. More focus on what actually happened in practice. Did the workflow run? Did it adapt when inputs were messy?
